# N16: One set of numbers: a metric’s row in the library counts the goals its page lists, status by status

A check of the Metric library module ([its section](../README.md#journeys-and-checks)): not a journey with steps a person takes, but a script that opens pages and reports what is wrong (Faro’s `evals/notes/16-metrics.cjs`). A rebuild proves the same by hand or with its own script: every failure below must not happen. Each is in the script’s words; {…} is what it measured.

## What it checks

one set of numbers in the metric library (ML1, docs/design/metrics/spec.md section 6). run({ open }) returns a list of failures. For every metric in the demo's library, as an admin on a computer: its row's goals by status are its page's table's rows, status by status; "No goals yet" on the row is "No goal uses this metric yet." on the page; and "See its goal" / "See its {n} goals" opens Goals filtered to the metric (ML2), which counts the same goals.

## Where it looks

- 1440 × 900, as amara, at `/metrics`

A width of 390 is a phone, 1440 (or 1280) a desktop; the address is in the demo on Thursday 5 November 2026 unless it names another day.

## What it reports as wrong

- the library lists {rows.length} metrics, not the demo’s 13
- {r.name}: its row says “{row || 'no goals'}”, its page lists “{page || 'no goals'}”
- {r.name}: its row says {r.none ? 'No goals yet' : 'it has goals'}, its page lists {statuses.length}
- {r.name}: its page’s heading says “{heading}” for {statuses.length} rows
- {r.name}: “See its goals” leads to {see}, not Goals filtered to it
- {r.name}: Goals filtered to it says “{line}”, its page lists {statuses.length}
